answer.text: Government spending more and taxing less to stimulate the economy
Government spending less and taxing more to cool the economy

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook explains that during recessions or a slow-moving economy, an expansionary fiscal policy means the government spends more and taxes less, leaving more money with citizens and corporates and resulting in fiscal deficits. The Trap: Spending less and taxing more is contractionary fiscal policy. Raising interest rates and reducing the money supply are monetary-policy levers used by the central bank, not fiscal-policy actions of the government. Note: The expansionary fiscal policy concept — more spending, less taxes and the resulting fiscal deficit — is covered on pages 97-98 of the NISM-Series-XV Research Analyst Certification Examination workbook (February 2026).
